**No.** The latest assessment, run on 12 November 2026, detected **13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025**, or 3.91% of the property. The JRC reference classified 98% of the affected area as forest in 2020.

The June 2025 assessment only had observations through 2024, so its “no loss detected” finding did not cover the newly reported 2025 loss. The annual data do not establish whether the loss occurred before or after the June assessment.

The latest series ends in 2025. Also, because no later year was observed, the event does not yet meet the tool’s stated corroboration rule. The due-diligence file should be updated and the event investigated.
